# Maximizing the Mostar index for bipartite graphs and split graphs

Author links open overlay panel Štefko Miklavič ^{a}, Johannes Pardey ^{b}, Dieter Rautenbach ^{b}, Florian Werner ^{b}

10.1016/j.disopt.2023.100768

## Abstract

Došlić et al. defined the Mostar index of a graph $G$ as $\sum _{uv\in E\left(G\right)}\phantom{\rule{-0.16667em}{0ex}}|{n}_{G}(u,v)-{n}_{G}(v,u)|$, where, for an edge $uv$ of $G$, the term ${n}_{G}(u,v)$ denotes the number of vertices of $G$ that have a smaller distance in $G$ to $u$ than to $v$. Contributing to conjectures posed by Došlić et al., we show that the Mostar index of bipartite graphs of order $n$ is at most $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{18}{n}^{3}$, and that the Mostar index of split graphs of order $n$ is at most $\frac{4}{27}{n}^{3}$.

## Introduction

Došlić et al. [1] defined the Mostar index $Mo\left(G\right)$ of a graph $G$ as $$Mo\left(G\right)=\sum _{uv\in E\left(G\right)}|{n}_{G}(u,v)-{n}_{G}(v,u)|,$$where, for an edge $uv$ of $G$, the term ${n}_{G}(u,v)$ denotes the number of vertices of $G$ that have a smaller distance in $G$ to $u$ than to $v$. They conjectured that the complete bipartite graph ${K}_{\lfloor n/3\rfloor ,n-\lfloor n/3\rfloor }$ has maximum Mostar index among all bipartite graphs of order $n$ (cf. [1, Conjecture 19]), and that ${S}_{\lfloor n/3\rfloor ,n-\lfloor n/3\rfloor }$ has maximum Mostar index among all graphs of order $n$ (cf. [1, Conjecture 20]), where ${S}_{k,n-k}$ denotes the split graph that arises from the disjoint union of a clique $C$ of order $k$ and an independent set $I$ of order $n-k$ by adding all possible edges between $C$ and $I$. The Mostar index of a complete bipartite graph ${K}_{\alpha n,(1-\alpha )n}$ with $\alpha \le \frac{1}{2}$ equals $\alpha (1-\alpha )(1-2\alpha ){n}^{3}$, which, considered as a function of $\alpha $, is maximized for ${\alpha }_{1}=\frac{1}{2}\left(1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)\approx 0.21132$. As observed by Geneson and Tsai [2], this means that, for sufficiently large $n$, Conjecture 19 from [1] does not hold, because the Mostar index of ${K}_{\lfloor {\alpha }_{1}n\rfloor ,n-\lfloor {\alpha }_{1}n\rfloor }$ is larger than that of ${K}_{\lfloor n/3\rfloor ,n-\lfloor n/3\rfloor }$.

Since its introduction in 2018 the Mostar index has already incited a lot of research, mostly concerning sparse graphs and trees [3], [4], [5], [6], [7], [8], chemical graphs [9], [10], [11], [12], [13], and hypercube-related graphs [14], [15], see also the recent survey [16]. However, the two mentioned conjectures from [1] remained open, which suggests that they are difficult. In fact, they do not seem amenable to the usual transformation arguments that modify a given graph iteratively. An interesting feature of the Mostar index in dense graphs is that, in order to maximize it, it seems plausible to have many edges. If the graphs get too dense though, then the contribution of each individual edge to the Mostar index tends to decrease. Therefore, maximizing the Mostar index over a class of possibly dense graphs requires a delicate balance between the total number of edges and the average contribution per edge.

In this paper we contribute to the above mentioned conjectures by proving the following two theorems.

Theorem 1

If $G$ is a bipartite graph of order $n$, then $$Mo\left(G\right)\le {\alpha }_{1}(1-{\alpha }_{1})(1-2{\alpha }_{1}){n}^{3}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{18}{n}^{3}\approx 0.096225{n}^{3}.$$

By the above discussion, Theorem 1 is best possible up to terms of order $O\left({n}^{2}\right)$. In particular, the factor $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{18}$ is best possible.

Theorem 2

If $G$ is a split graph that arises from a clique $C$ of order $\alpha n$ and an independent set $I$ of order $(1-\alpha )n$ for some $\alpha \in [0,1]$ by adding $m$ edges between vertices in $C$ and vertices in $I$, then $$Mo\left(G\right)\le ((1+\alpha )n-1)m-\frac{2{m}^{2}}{(1-\alpha )n}\le \left\{\begin{array}{cc}\alpha (1-\alpha ){n}^{2}\left((1-\alpha )n-1\right)\phantom{\rule{1em}{0ex}}\hfill & \text{, if }\alpha \le \frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{3n}\text{,}\hfill \\ \frac{1}{8}(1-\alpha )n{\left((1+\alpha )n-1\right)}^{2}\phantom{\rule{1em}{0ex}}\hfill & \text{, if }\alpha >\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{3n}\hfill \end{array}\right.\le \frac{4}{27}{n}^{3}.$$

Each bound stated in Theorem 2 is best possible up to terms of lower order. More precisely, for each stated bound, say $b(n,\alpha ,m)$, there are graphs $G$ of arbitrarily large order $n$ with $Mo\left(G\right)\ge b(n,\alpha ,m)-O\left({n}^{2}\right)$.

All proofs are given in the next section.

Our proofs rely on relaxations of the Mostar index, linear programming, duality, and arguments from optimization theory.
